subject: Interim notice: elevated 503s from rw-eval-7b — mitigation & timeline
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, ops@clearcommerce.com
Date: 2026-10-21 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: rw-eval-7b — surge in 503s observed (preliminary)

Team / Claire,

We just detected an increase in 503/timeout responses for rw-eval-7b serving the ClearCommerce account starting ~08:45 PDT. Error rate for that model on their route is ~12% (was <0.5% baseline). Latency for successful calls is also elevated (~2.1s median -> ~4.8s).

Immediate actions taken: 
- Redirected 30% of traffic to a warmed fallback model variant (rw-eval-7b-cold) to reduce impact.
- Kicked a diagnostic snapshot and current request traces (attached).
- Placed an ops page for on-call.

Root-cause hypothesis is an interaction between a kernel memory leak on a specific host family and request-bursting patterns from the customer's peak queries; engineering is continuing triage.

Claire — I cc'd you so you're aware while we validate. Marissa, can you prepare a short external note for the customer with expected timeline? Sean, want you to oversee customer comms and approvals for a temporary credit if impacts persist beyond 6 hours.

Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Claire Wu <ops@clearcommerce.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21 09:35 AM -0700
Subject: Re: rw-eval-7b — surge in 503s observed (preliminary)

Thanks for the quick heads-up, Hannah. We're seeing failures sporadically across our batch jobs and a handful of user-facing failures. Our engineers are holding off retries per your suggestion — please keep us posted if you need any logs or request traces from our side.

Two asks from us:
1) Can you confirm whether our data or prompt shapes could be contributing?
2) If this will be a prolonged outage, we may need a short-term mitigation plan so our payment flows don't fail.

Appreciate the rapid response.

Claire
Ops Lead, ClearCommerce
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wu <ops@clearcommerce.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21 10:05 AM -0700
Subject: RE: rw-eval-7b — surge in 503s observed (preliminary)

Claire — thanks for confirming. Short answers up front:
- We don't see any malformed requests on your traces; payloads and prompt shapes match the usual profile.
- The immediate mitigation is traffic routing to the warmed fallback and aggressive retries on server-side where idempotent. We're coordinating with ClearCommerce engineering on safe retry guidance.

Planned next steps and timeline (aiming for staged recovery):
1) 10:15 — full host pool rolling restart for the affected cluster (ongoing).
2) 10:45 — monitoring window to observe error rate; if >1% we will increase fallback routing to 60%.
3) 13:00 — engineering-led kernel patch + redeploy; expect narrow maintenance window (~15–30 mins) with automatic failover.

Contingencies: if we cannot reduce to <1% by 13:30, we'll propose a service credit and a short-term arrangement to lower traffic priority for non-critical jobs. Marissa, please draft a customer-facing note with these items and a brief FAQ. Neha, can you attach the diagnostic snapshot and open an INF ticket with priority P1?

Claire — I will keep you updated at each milestone and will send a concise recovery note once we've validated.

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: support_ticket_CC-4781.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wu <ops@clearcommerce.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21 04:38 PM -0700
Subject: Update & recovery: rw-eval-7b — issue mitigated, validation complete

Claire — quick update from the incident today.

What happened (short): a kernel-level memory fragmentation bug on a specific host family caused transient 503s for rw-eval-7b when a sustained burst of short requests exhausted ephemeral allocator pools. The bug surfaced at your morning peak and pushed the error rate up to ~12%.

What we did: 
- Immediately diverted traffic to a warmed fallback (reduced customer-facing errors within 20 minutes).
- Performed a rolling restart of the affected serving hosts and applied a memory-safeguard kernel parameter.
- Deployed a targeted runtime patch (INF-5921) at 13:10 PDT; the patch addressed the allocator behavior for the workload shape we saw.

Status now: 
- Error rate for your routes is back down to baseline (~0.3%).
- Latency has returned to normal medians.
- Continued monitoring at 30m cadence for the next 24 hours.

Customer impact & remediation: 
- We know there were failed payment attempts; we recommend your retry policy to run delayed retries with exponential backoff for 2–4 minutes where idempotent.
- As a goodwill gesture, we're prepared to issue a one-time service credit for the impacted window. Sean will follow up on the credit and any SLA considerations.

Attachments: diagnostic_snapshot_20261021.log (trimmed).

If you want a technical write-up (postmortem with traces and timeline), we can provide a short incident report within 48 hours and a detailed postmortem in 7–10 business days. Would you prefer a short technical digest or the full postmortem?

Apologies for the disruption — we appreciate your patience and will follow up with the incident report.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
